front: Group
back: Combines related members of a field into a single member, such as merging city spellings into one.

front: Three ways to create a group
back: Select marks or headers and click the group icon (a paperclip) on the tooltip or the toolbar. Or, in the Data pane, right-click a field and select Create > Group.

front: How do you edit or undo a group later?
back: Right-click the group field and choose Edit Group. Select members and click Ungroup to take them out.

front: What does Include 'Other' do in the Edit Group dialog?
back: It puts all remaining, non-grouped members in an Other group. Use it to keep a few named groups and lump the long tail together.

front: Set
back: A custom field that defines a subset of data based on some conditions. Every member is either In the set or Out of it.

front: Fixed set vs. dynamic set
back: A fixed set's members do not change, even if the data changes. A dynamic set's members change when the underlying data changes.

front: How do you create a fixed set, and how a dynamic set?
back: Fixed: right-click marks and select Create Set. Dynamic: in the Data pane, right-click a dimension and select Create > Set, then use the General, Condition or Top tab.

front: Which dialog tabs define a dynamic set?
back: General (pick values or Use all), Condition (rules, for example on a measure) and Top (limits, such as the top N by a measure).

front: How do you show a set as In and Out categories?
back: Right-click the set and choose Show In/Out of Set. Show Members in Set shows the members instead.

front: Hierarchy
back: Several related dimensions stacked from general to detailed, so you can drill down and up in the view.

front: How do you create a hierarchy in the Data pane?
back: Drag a field and drop it directly on top of another field, then name the hierarchy. Drag more fields into it in order, general to detailed.

front: How do you drill down or up a hierarchy in the view?
back: Click the + or - icon on the hierarchy field. Drilling down adds the next field as nested headers.

front: Group vs. set vs. hierarchy: which fits which job?
back: Merging spellings is a group. "Top 10 customers" is a set (or a Top filter). Category > Sub-Category drilling is a hierarchy.

front: Where do you drag a field to filter a view?
back: To the Filters shelf. The Filter dialog opens when you add it.

front: What are the four tabs of a dimension filter?
back: General (tick members), Wildcard (match text), Condition (a rule on a measure) and Top (top or bottom N by a measure).

front: In what order does Tableau apply filters?
back: Extract filters, data source filters, context filters, dimension filters, then measure filters. Table calculation filters are applied last.

front: How do you make a dimension filter run first?
back: Right-click it and choose Add to Context. Context filters appear at the top of the Filters shelf and are gray.

front: A Top N filter ignores another dimension filter. What is the fix?
back: Add the other filter to context so it runs first. Dimension filters, including Top N, otherwise run at the same stage.

front: How do you let viewers filter a sheet themselves?
back: Open the field's drop-down menu and select Show Filter to put a filter card on the sheet.

front: What is a measure filter applied to?
back: The aggregated value of each mark (like SQL's `HAVING`). You choose the aggregation, then Range of Values, At Least, At Most or Special.

front: Relative date filter vs. range of dates filter
back: Relative: a range that updates with the date you open the view, such as the last 3 months. Range of dates: a fixed range, or only a starting or ending date.

front: "Show every December": which date filter?
back: A date-part filter (Months). If you select Quarters, you can choose to filter specific quarters.

front: "Always show the last 30 days": which date filter?
back: A relative date filter. "Show 1 January to 31 March 2025" is a range of dates.

front: What does the Special option of a date filter offer?
back: Null dates, non-null dates, or all dates.
